subject: SOC 2 scope question — network zones & PrivateLink applicability

Cc: security@proofpoint.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II scope — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC questions

Sean —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our security team is working through Redwood's SOC 2 Type II applicability and we have a couple of clarifying questions before we finalize the vendor assessment:

1) Does the SOC 2 Type II report cover requests routed to Redwood Hosted API only, or does it also include Dedicated (customer-reserved GPU pools) and Private (VPC / customer-managed connectors) deployments?

2) For Dedicated pools that are physically isolated but still operated by Redwood, do we need a separate bridge letter or is the standard Type II coverage sufficient?

3) For PrivateLink / VPC-onboarded customers where traffic goes over a customer-managed network and we do not manage VM/infra, what evidence will Redwood provide for the SOC 2 controls (network controls, logging, change management)?

Attached is our SIG/CAIQ worksheet with the specific questions where we need evidence pointers. Can you confirm who on your side owns the evidence collection and whether you can provide a bridge letter where required?

Thanks,
Sarah White
Security Operations
Proofpoint

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II scope — hosted vs dedicated vs VPC questions

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the worksheet — received it and starting a pass. Short answers up front so you can proceed with your assessment:

- Hosted API: in-scope in our current SOC 2 Type II report.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed pools): generally in-scope when the pool is fully operated/managed by Redwood and tenant isolation controls are in place.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: not automatically in-scope — coverage depends on whether the control plane and ownership are within Redwood's managed boundary or if the customer owns the infrastructure.

I want to loop in our security/compliance lead and the engineering manager who owns deployment topology so we can give concrete evidence paths (network diagrams, logging extracts, bridge language). Will forward to them now.

—Sean

Thanks Sean — that is helpful. A few clarifying bullets from our side so your compliance team can target evidence:

- For Dedicated pools: we need confirmation that tenant isolation controls (network ACLs, hypervisor/host separation, RBAC for operator access) are exercised and audited during the Type II period. A bridge letter would be acceptable if some host-level artifacts are excluded from the report, but we'd prefer inclusion if feasible.
- For Private/VPC: Proofpoint's policy is to treat anything that touches customer-managed networks as out-of-scope for vendor SOC unless the vendor explicitly states coverage. If a bridge letter is possible to attest to the controls Redwood executes (e.g., code deployments, audit logging ingestion into customer SIEM, runbook-based access controls), that would reduce our follow-up ask.

I've flagged the SIG sheet rows 12–29 as high priority. Happy to take a short call next week to walk through specifics.

—Sarah

Thanks Sean — quick summary and recommended text we can provide to Proofpoint. Long version below; pasteable bridge language at the end.

Summary (control applicability):
- Hosted API (redwood-managed endpoints): fully in-scope for our current SOC 2 Type II report. Auditors sampled production nodes, change management pipelines, and access logs during the reporting window.
- Dedicated pools (Redwood-managed): in-scope when the GPU pools are provisioned and operated by Redwood (tenant mapping, RBAC, operator access controls, and network ACLs are within our control plane). Auditors included a sampling of dedicated pools where evidence was available; where a dedicated deployment was customer-managed (rare), that instance was excluded.
- Private/VPC / customer-managed connectors: out-of-scope by default for the SOC 2 engagement because the customer manages the underlying network and compute. However, we can provide a SOC 2 bridge letter that:
  - Describes the Redwood controls that remain in effect (application-level logging, deployment change controls, code review, operator RBAC)
  - Identifies customer responsibilities (VPC routing, security groups, host hardening)
  - Explains the boundary of audit evidence (what auditors tested vs what is customer-maintained)

Evidence we can provide for Proofpoint immediately:
- Copy of the SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) — covers Hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated pools where sampled
- Tenant mapping playbook (we can export tenant isolation evidence and sampling notes)
- Network diagram showing boundaries and data flows (I reviewed Sean's draft; will finalize)
- A draft bridge letter template that they can include in their assessment package

Draft bridge letter snippet (paste into Proofpoint assessment):
"Redwood Inference maintains responsibility for the application layer, deployment pipelines, and operator access controls for Hosted and Redwood-managed Dedicated deployments. When a customer elects a Private/VPC deployment in which the customer retains control of network and compute resources, those specific host- and network-level controls are customer-managed and outside Redwood's SOC 2 audit boundary. Redwood can provide a bridge letter attesting to the controls we continue to operate (deployment approvals, application logging, and access management) and will collaborate with the customer to identify complementary evidence for joint control areas."
Next steps I propose: 
1) We send Proofpoint the SOC 2 report and draft bridge letter + tenant mapping playbook.
2) Offer a 30-minute call to walk through their SIG rows (I can join).

I've attached the tenant mapping playbook and a cleaned-up network diagram. Happy to iterate.

—KImberly Park
Head of Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
